cards.text: One afternoon, Peter and John, two of Jesus' apostles, are heading up to the temple. It's the hour of prayer, the ninth hour. Nothing special. Just two friends going to pray. Friend, that's usually when God likes to show up.
Meanwhile, a man who's been lame from birth is being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful. Every single day they set him down there to beg from the people going in.

cards.question: The lame man at the gate called Beautiful sees Peter and John about to go in. What does he ask them for?

cards.text: Peter looks right at him, and so does John. Then Peter says, "Look at us!" I bet this man has spent all day looking at feet walking past. Now somebody wants EYE CONTACT.

cards.question: The lame man gives Peter and John his attention. What is he expecting?

answers.text: To be told to move along

cards.text: Then Peter says, "Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you." Friend, if I had my hand out and somebody opened with "I have no money," my mustache would already be waving goodbye.

cards.question: Peter has no silver or gold for the lame man. In whose name does Peter tell him to get up and walk?

cards.text: Peter takes the man by the right hand and helps him up.

cards.question: Once Peter helps him up, the lame man's feet and ankles get strong slowly over the next few days.

cards.text: He SPRINGS to his feet and starts walking. This man has been sitting since BIRTH, and he springs up. I bend over to pick up one dropped chocolate chip and I need a minute, a deep breath and a pep talk.

cards.question: The man who was lame can walk now. Where does he go with Peter and John?
In the temple courts, the healed man is walking and leaping. What else is he doing?

cards.text: Now all the people see him walking and praising God. And they know that face.

cards.question: The people in the temple courts recognize the man walking and praising God. Who do they know him as?

answers.text: The man who begged at the Beautiful Gate
A servant of the high priest

cards.question: When the people see the man who used to beg, they're filled with wonder and amazement at what happened to him.

cards.text: The man clings to Peter and John. I bet you couldn't pry him off those two with a spatula.

cards.question: All the astonished people come running to Peter and John in the walkway called ___ Colonnade.

cards.text: Peter sees the whole crowd staring at him and John like they just pulled a rabbit out of a chef's hat. So he speaks up: "Men of Israel, why are you surprised by this?"

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd that he and John made the man walk by their own power and godliness.

cards.text: Peter says the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of their fathers, has glorified His servant Jesus. Then he reminds them they handed Jesus over and rejected Him before Pilate, the Roman governor.

cards.question: Peter brings up Pilate. What had Pilate decided to do with Jesus?

cards.text: Peter calls Jesus the Holy and Righteous One. And he says they rejected Him and asked for somebody else to be set free instead.

cards.question: Instead of the Holy and Righteous One, who does Peter say the people asked to be released?

cards.text: Peter doesn't tiptoe around it. He says they killed the Author of life, but God raised Him from the dead.

cards.question: Peter says he and John are witnesses that God raised Jesus from the dead.
Peter points to the man the crowd sees and knows. How does Peter say this man was made strong?

answers.text: By faith in the name of Jesus
By the prayers of the priests
By a gift from the temple

cards.text: Then Peter's voice gets gentle. "And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your leaders."

cards.question: Peter says God fulfilled what He foretold through all the prophets about His Christ. What did the prophets say would happen to the Christ?
So what does Peter tell the crowd to do, so that their sins may be wiped away?

cards.text: Peter says times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and He may send Jesus, the Christ, appointed for them. But heaven must take Him in until the time comes for the restoration of all things, which God announced long ago through His holy prophets.
Then Peter quotes Moses, Israel's great leader. Moses said, "The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers."

cards.question: Moses said God would raise up a prophet like him. What did Moses say the people must do?

answers.text: Listen to Him in everything He says
Build Him a brand new temple
Wait for Him to show a sign

cards.text: And Moses didn't sugarcoat the other side either. Everyone who doesn't listen to Him will be completely cut off from among his people.

cards.question: Peter says Moses was the only prophet who ever spoke about these days.

cards.text: Peter tells them they're sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with their fathers. God said to Abraham, "Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed."

cards.question: Peter says God raised up His Servant and sent Him to the crowd first to bless them. How does Peter say He blesses them?

answers.text: By turning each of them from their wicked ways
By giving each of them silver and gold
By making each of them rulers of nations

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now, friend. Trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "I have no money", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: 'One afternoon…', 'It's the hour of prayer…', 'Nothing special.', 'Just two friends going to pray.' and 'Friend, that's usually…'.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: 'Friend, that's usually when God likes to show up' is a general claim about how God works. It isn't in the passage and has no reference, so it adds a fact rather than just carrying the moment.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'Peter looks right at him…', 'Then Peter says…', 'I bet this man…' and 'Now somebody wants EYE CONTACT.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is a bare restatement of the verse, with none of Papa Dorin's voice: 'Peter takes the man by the right hand and helps him up.'

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'He SPRINGS…', 'This man has been sitting since BIRTH…' and 'I bend over…'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'This man has been sitting since BIRTH' is stated as a fact. The text says he was lame from birth (Acts 3:2) and used to sit begging (Acts 3:10). It never says he had been sitting since birth.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answers 'Home to his family' and 'Out through the city gate' are generic. Neither is a real detail from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The card cites Acts 3:9, but 'And they know that face' tells the recognition in Acts 3:10. The citation should be Acts 3:9-10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the 9 choice cards (with 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank), so it dominates the stop.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 7 of the 10 choice cards, with 3 true or false and no fill in the blank, so it dominates the stop. Both stops also lean heavily on multiple choice in the same way.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: After card 1, the story cards are almost all flat retellings with little of Papa Dorin's voice or humor. Cards 3, 5, 13 and 18 read like the verses restated, and card 13 closely tracks the BSB wording of Acts 3:20-21.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card says 'Peter says he and John are witnesses.' Acts 3:15 says only 'we are witnesses' and doesn't say who 'we' is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story-continues line nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Stop 1 card 1 ('two of Jesus' apostles') and stop 2 card 3 ('Pilate, the Roman governor') state facts from outside the passage. The docs say such facts come 'with their reference,' but each card's verses field may only cite the passage verses it tells, 'no wider and no narrower.' The JSON has no other place for an outside reference.
findings.question: How should a card cite a fact from outside the passage, such as who a new person is? Should it go in the verses field, in the card text, or nowhere, given the 'no wider and no narrower' rule?

findings.problem: The last story card is only the story-continues line and tells no verse, but its verses field cites Acts 3:26. The docs allow this kind of card when the last verse was asked on a choice card, but they don't say what it should cite.
findings.question: What should the verses field be for a final story card that is only the story-continues line and tells no verses?
